title: Risk calibration runway and KPI breadcrumbs
summary: A hypothesis-driven runway tracker designed to surface KPI breadcrumbs across phased launches. Combines a rolling roadmap (spiral milestones), explicit acceptance gates, smoke tests, and contingency mappings for Dedicated + Hosted rollouts.
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an operational instrument for product ops and release leads to: 1) track the next 6 sprint milestones as a spiral/iterative runway, 2) attach measurable KPI breadcrumbs (leading signals and lagging outcomes) to each milestone, and 3) define launch acceptance gates, smoke tests, and fallback owners for quick go/no-go decisions.

How to use:
- Update the "Spiral milestones" section weekly during product-ops sync.
- Each milestone MUST have a hypothesis, a primary KPI (leading), an SLA/threshold, an owner, and a fallback plan.
- Use the "Smoke test matrix" in the 24h pre-launch window; record results and mark pass/fail in the heatmap.

1) Spiral milestones (6-sprint runway)
Format: Sprint | Hypothesis ID | Mission | Primary leading KPI (target) | Lag KPI (acceptance) | Owner | Escalation/Fallback
S1 | HYP-001 | Canary routing + autoscale probe | 95th p50 latency < 220ms (per-route) | Error rate < 0.25% | Caroline Turner | SRE oncall -> scale-policy rollback
S2 | HYP-002 | KV prefix cache effectiveness | Cache hit rate >= 18% | Token cost/unit down 8% | Diego Alvarez | Roll to quantized model variant
S3 | HYP-003 | Cost-aware routing (tiered) | % of routed cheap-variant >= 30% | Avg cost/token <= $0.0009 | Asha Mehta | Throttle non-critical routes
S4 | HYP-004 | Dedicated capacity soak (shard stability) | Sustained qps within 90% of committed | Queueing time < 80ms | Ravi Shah | Add burst nodes + throttle API clients
S5 | HYP-005 | Private deployment ingress verification | End-to-end auth latency < 150ms | Audit log completeness 100% | Maya Patel | Hold deployment and escalate to security
S6 | HYP-006 | Rollout to 10% of paid customers | Adoption conversion >= 12% | SLA complaints < 2/week | Product Operations Lead | Scheduled rollback slot

2) KPI breadcrumbs (leading signals -> corrective actions)
Design: For each leading KPI we keep a short breadcrumb (signal, window, alerting rule, immediate action).
Example entry:
- Cache hit rate (HYP-002): signal = 5m moving avg, window = 30m, alert = drop below 12% -> immediate action = increase warmup, enable aggressive prefetch; owner = caching eng lead.
- 95th p50 latency (HYP-001): signal = p95 trailing hour across primary region, alert if >220ms for 10m -> action = divert to replica region + enable smaller batch size; owner = serving-runtime eng.

3) Acceptance gates (go/no-go checklist)
Pre-flight category checklist (ALL items must be green for go):
- Functional: Top 10 end-to-end flows pass smoke harness (see matrix)
- Latency: p95 vs target (per-route) within threshold for 1h under expected pilot load
- Errors: 0 critical errors, <0.5% client-visible errors
- Observability: Tracing + token-level costing enabled; dashboards populated
- Security & Compliance: KMS keys present, audit ingest validated (for Private)
- Support readiness: Escalation contacts available and on-call roster confirmed

4) Smoke test matrix (24h pre-launch)
Columns: Test ID | Flow | Expected metric | Pass criteria | Run owner | Result (pass/fail) | Notes\ST-01 | Auth+Token exchange | Latency <120ms | pass if <120ms across 100 samples | Maya Patel | pending | run after staging sync\ST-02 | Short-text generation | p50 < 180ms and coherence check > 90% | pass if both met | Diego Alvarez | pending | run at 03:00 PST\ST-03 | Embeddings batch path | throughput >= 250 rps | pass if >= 250 sustained 2m | Caroline Turner | pending | check dedicated pool

5) SLA burn and surge scenarios
- SLA burn tracker: projection of committed throughput vs observed qps. Add a column for 'surge buffer' (committed * 1.25). If observed > surge buffer for >15m, trigger surge playbook.
- Surge playbook shortform: Throttle low-priority tenant traffic -> switch to cached responses for stable flows -> auto-scale extra dedicated nodes -> notify customers on status page.

6) Contingency mapping (owner ladder)
Per subsystem list (serving-runtime, routing, autoscaler, infra, security) map primary -> secondary -> fallback contact and fallback action. Keep phone numbers in the private runbook; in this sheet keep the on-call rotation token and escalate steps.
Example: Serving-runtime: primary = Diego Alvarez, secondary = Priya Nair, fallback = SRE oncall (rotate). Fallback action = disable batch fusion and revert to last-stable kernels.

7) Communication & public-facing copy (first-3-lines)
- Status page blurb (short): "We’re initiating a gradual rollout of the new inference routing. You may see transient latency variation for 10–15 minutes; we’ll post updates here."
- Customer escalation template subject: "[Action required] Change in inference routing affecting your traffic" with required fields: impact, mitigation, ETA, contact.

8) Quick metrics snapshot (examples you should paste in during sync)
- Live sample: total qps: 4,320 | avg cost/token: $0.00105 | p95 latency: 198ms | error rate: 0.21%
- Acceptance quick-check: rolling 10m p95 vs target: OK / AT-RISK / FAIL (choose one)

9) Open questions & decision log (short bullets)
- Do we force-fail routes that exceed token-cost budget or allow temporary overrun and bill back? (assigned: Ravi Shah)
- Define what constitutes a "critical error" for this rollout (assigned: SRE + Product Ops)

10) Action items (next 7 days)
- Diego: run cache warmup experiment and post results to linked Confluence (due 2025-02-20)
- Asha: finalize tiered routing thresholds and update routing policy (due 2025-02-18)
- Maya: confirm security audit for private deploys and attach artifact (due 2025-02-22)
- Product Ops: schedule 24h pre-launch smoke run and confirm on-call rota (due 2025-02-28)

Appendix - minimal table export (CSV-ready)

Notes: keep this doc minimal and lightweight. If a milestone becomes stale (no updates for 10 days) mark as "stale" and create a follow-up ticket. Prefer short, measurable breadcrumbs over long narratives.
notes: Created as a pragmatic sheet to bridge product ops and infra teams during launches; intended as a living document (weekly cadence).
